subject: spaceGalley
pitch:
Category: Prop group.
Subject: spaceship galley kitchen.
Style: Alien (1979) Nostromo.
reasoning:
I'm planning a single TypeScript module for a static Nostromo-style galley kitchen prop group, working in model space without needing joints since it's a non-articulated static model. I'm sketching out the layout: a floor deck plate at ground level plus a back wall panel, keeping the design efficient but detailed.

Now I'm fleshing out the full scene — counter with stainless top, locker cabinets with handles, a stove with pots, sink, overhead cabinet, a central mess table with bench stools, coffee machine, fridge, ceiling pipes, warning-light strip, a glowing green CRT monitor, hanging cups, and a Jonesy cat bowl, plus SVG label textures like "NOSTROMO" and hazard stripes. I'm working out real-world proportions (3.2m wide galley, 0.9m counter height, back wall at z=-0.9, table at z=0.5) and planning to use box-geometry helper functions along with imported paint and metal materials from the clockwork and glow kits.

I'm sketching helper functions for boxes and textured plates, then laying out the room piece by piece — starting with the floor as a thin hazard-striped box and the back wall as a larger panel behind it.

For side walls, I'm thinking of keeping one wall simple with a round hatch made from a torus and disc, and a ceiling slab capping the whole structure.

Now I'm adding ceiling pipes and glowing light panels, then building a counter cabinet along the wall with paneled doors, handles, label plates, and a steel countertop, followed by a sink with a recessed basin and curved faucet.

For the hob I'm placing four burner rings with a pot and kettle nearby, a tall fridge-freezer unit with a glowing display panel, wall cabinets above the counter with hazard-strip labels, and a hanging rail with hooks for ladles and cups against a steel backsplash.

Then I'm adding a monitor on an arm above the fridge, tilted slightly, and designing the central table with a steel top, pedestal legs, and two long benches with orange-red vinyl seating.

Now I'm placing table items like compartmented trays, cylindrical cups, a cat bowl, coffee pot, salt shaker, labeled food cans, and tray cards, plus a glowing coffee machine on the counter. I'm adding a hazard-stripe floor decal in front of the counter, amber glow strips along the cabinet bases, and wall decals reading "GALLEY" and the ship registration, along with a red fire extinguisher mounted on the wall.

Now I'm recomputing positions: fixing the fridge and counter spans, placing the extinguisher against the back wall within the galley's width, and adding a left end wall with a round bulkhead hatch made from a ring torus set into a wall box.

For the hatch, I'm orienting the torus flat in the XY plane with its axis along z, positioning it near the top of the wall, and checking it clears the bench and table. I'm also skipping the front wall for a cutaway view, adding a small coffee machine on the counter, a utensil rail instead of hanging pots, and applying a riveted panel texture to the back wall surface.

Cabinets get the panelled texture, steel parts use a metal shader, and the floor gets a darker panelled texture at a different scale, with a modest color palette to stay under the flat-color limit. For the faucet, pipes, hoses, and hanging cable, I'm using bezier and catmull-rom sweeps to create curved tube geometry with small radii.

Now I'm defining helper functions for boxes, cylinders, and decal planes to quickly place parts, orienting the cylinder axis along y by default and using a direction vector for horizontal placements.

Next I'm setting up a cabinet door function with a front plate and a handle rod, then starting on SVG textures like hazard stripes and a greenish terminal screen pattern for the sci-fi kitchen scene.

Still writing SVG textures...

Skipping cups, using a simple box instead; adding a steel tray with a texture plane on top oriented so its drawing faces correctly, and planning hazard stripe planes along the counter front edge.

I'm working out the cabinet geometry: body spanning y=0.05 to 0.9 with a darker toe-kick strip and amber glow accent near the base, positioning the cabinet depth between z=-0.85 and -0.25 so it sits just in front of the back wall at z=-0.9, leaving a small gap.

Now I'm laying out the door sections across the counter front at z=-0.25: sink doors on the left, a wider oven-style door with a glass panel and handle in the middle under the hob, and two more doors on the right near the coffee station, figuring out their x-centers and widths so they fit evenly within the 2.1-unit counter span.

Then I'm placing the steel countertop slab on top, adding a dark recessed sink basin, and sketching the faucet as a curved bezier path rising from the basin and arcing over toward the spout tip.

Now I'm laying out the stovetop: a black hob plate with four torus-shaped burner rings, making one glow red for a hot burner, plus adding a pot with lid and a pan with a handle on two of the burners, control dials on the backsplash, and a steel backsplash panel along the wall behind the stove.

I'm also placing a hanging rail with hooks for utensils like a ladle, and planning the wall cabinets above the counter with four evenly spaced doors across the width of the kitchen wall.

Now I'm adding label plates and handles to each cabinet door, plus a hazard warning strip positioned along the lower edge of the doors, an under-cabinet cool-white light strip for task lighting, and starting on the fridge body dimensions.

I'm designing the fridge further with two doors split by a seam line, vertical handle rods, a glowing display screen, and a logo plate on the lower door. Then I'm placing a fire extinguisher assembly near the fridge—red cylinder body, dark neck, nozzle, hose sweep, wall bracket, and a FIRE sign plate mounted above it—before starting a wall-mounted monitor arm positioned above the fridge.

Now I'm building the monitor itself with a CRT box, glowing front screen, support stand, and figuring out its placement relative to the fridge top, then moving on to the ceiling panel dimensions and how they align with the room's floor and wall boundaries.

Defining wall positions and ceiling pipe rods...

I'm placing two benches flanking the table at z=0 and z=1.2, each with seat, legs, and cushion, checking the knee gap against the table's half-width to make sure clearances work out fine.

Now adding table items on top: trays, cups, bowl, pot, cans, and salt/pepper shakers, skipping stools or extra chairs. Then I'm building a hatch on the left wall with a torus ring door frame, a disc for the door itself, a wheel handle made of crossing rods, and a "GALLEY" decal plate positioned above it, oriented so it's readable from the +x side.

I'm adding hazard warning stripes at the wall base near the hatch, then setting the floor as a dark paneled grating texture while skipping a floor drain. For the back wall I'm placing vertical conduit pipes with clamps at both corners, and adding a small LED switch panel with glowing red/green/amber indicators near the fridge area, positioned among the pipe conduits.

I'm reconsidering the LED panel placement since it collides with a pipe, deciding instead to put indicators on the fridge display and coffee machine rather than a separate panel. I'm designing a coffee machine on the counter with a body, back column, top head, base plate, and a dark amber glass pot on the warming plate.

Now I'm planning a utensils rail mounted on the wall between the counter and cabinets, spanning across the backsplash area, with hooks and hanging items like a ladle with a bowl-shaped end.

I'll add a spatula and alternate a few hanging utensils, maybe skip mugs and spice jars to keep things simple. I'm deciding against extra details like a clock or a screen on the wall, keeping focus on the main layout.

Now I'm finalizing the code structure, making sure the glow element types check out properly, and considering a subtle grime texture for the floor paint to add realism without overcomplicating things.

I'm writing a hazard-stripe SVG pattern made of repeating yellow-and-black parallelograms, then a small label helper that generates a rounded tag with bold monospace text for signage.
